wormald.shelfmark: 'Offa Bible': a sister-Bible of the Codex Amiatinus (fragments; Wormald gives no shelfmark)
wormald.wormald_origin: Made at Monkwearmouth/Jarrow and came to Worcester; perhaps the Bible Worcester believed King Offa had given; disintegrated before the Dissolution, when leaves of Bible and cartulary passed to the Willoughbys of Wollaton (p. 184 and n. 90).
wormald.other_contents: Bible; the eleventh-century Worcester cartulary was probably inserted into it (p. 184).
wormald.overview: A Bible made at Monkwearmouth/Jarrow as a companion of the Codex Amiatinus, which reached Worcester and probably had the eleventh-century cathedral cartulary bound into it. If the IV Edgar leaves now in Nero E.i were lodged in that cartulary, as Wormald suggests, the code would for a time have been kept inside this Bible. It fell apart before the Dissolution, and some of its leaves went to the Willoughby family at Wollaton.
wormald.key_quote: 'It was probably inserted into one of the two great sister-Bibles of the Codex Amiatinus' (p. 184)
wormald.doubts: No laws; not in guide. Context for Nero E.i only. Wormald gives no shelfmark.
verify_notes: Checked p. 184 and nn. 89–90; minor rewording of origin, otherwise no changes.
